headline: Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook and Teams worldwide
summary: A widespread Microsoft 365 outage on November 12 knocked out Outlook, Teams, Intune and other services for about a day, hitting governments, hospitals and schools. Microsoft later said the cause was a July software defect, not a cyberattack, and said service was fully restored.

claims.statement: A major Microsoft 365 outage began on November 12, disrupting Outlook and other services worldwide.

sources.quote: Microsoft’s Outlook email hit by new outage
Multiple Microsoft 365 services are experiencing an outage
Massive Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot worldwide

claims.statement: Microsoft initially attributed the disruption to elevated load on its infrastructure.

sources.quote: "elevated load" issues.
experiencing “elevated loads”

claims.statement: The outage also took down Microsoft Intune and Exchange Online.

sources.quote: taken down email and Intune
damaged Exchange Online and services that rely on it

claims.statement: The disruption affected governments, hospitals and schools around the world.

sources.quote: Governments, hospitals, courts scrambled by global Microsoft outage.
The House of Representatives, health care providers, schools and many other organizations were affected.

claims.statement: Microsoft said the outage was not caused by a cyberattack.

sources.quote: the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident
a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash

claims.statement: Earlier in the incident, Microsoft had not ruled out a cyberattack as the cause.

sources.quote: Hasn't completely ruled out cyberattack as cause

claims.statement: Microsoft apologized for the outage, saying it was 'deeply sorry'.

sources.quote: Microsoft has apologised for the issue
company says it's 'deeply sorry'

claims.statement: Microsoft said services were fully restored to all affected customers.

sources.quote: The company restored service to email and other Microsoft 365 and related services to all customers by Friday night
Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage hits governments

claims.statement: One estimate put the economic cost of the outage at $7 billion.

sources.quote: One think tank’s estimate puts the cost of the outage at $7 billion.

claims.statement: Workers in Japan resorted to fax machines to cope with the outage.

sources.quote: Japanese workers are breaking out fax machines to deal with Microsoft's 365 outage.

claims.statement: Microsoft later said the outage was caused by a software defect introduced in a July update, which triggered a cascading failure across its networking gateway servers.

sources.quote: Microsoft blames monster email outage on software defect introduced in July fix
triggering a cascading failure that left more than 80% of its networking gateway servers unresponsive.

claims.statement: The outage was later linked to a chlorine gas poisoning incident at a hotel after a safety warning system that relied on Outlook failed.

sources.quote: Microsoft 365 outage leads to chlorine gas poisoning of 15 hotel guests
A safety warning went missing, chemical levels soared, and five guests ended up in hospital

discrepancies.explanation: The Register reported Microsoft had not ruled out a cyberattack, while the BBC and Wired reported Microsoft had already ruled a cyberattack out as the cause.

quotes.quote: Hasn't completely ruled out cyberattack as cause
the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident
